chunks: Visiting the graves of the Imams al-Ḥasan ibn ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib, ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥusayn, Muḥammad ibn ʿAlī al-Bāqir, and Jaʿfar ibn Muḥammad al-Ṣādiq, peace be upon them, in al-Baqīʿ.
When you come to the graves of the Imams, peace be upon them, in al-Baqīʿ, place them before you, then say:

Peace be upon you, O Imams of guidance. Peace be upon you, O people of taqwa. Peace be upon you, O proofs of Allah upon the people of the world. Peace be upon you, O you who uphold justice among creation. Peace be upon you, O people of purity. Peace be upon you, O people of intimate divine counsel. I bear witness that you conveyed, gave sincere counsel, and were patient in the way of Allah, Mighty and Exalted, and you were denied. Wrong was done to you, yet you forgave. I bear witness that you are the rightly guided Imams, that obedience to you is obligatory, that your word is truth, and that you called yet were not answered, and you commanded yet were not obeyed. You are the supports of the religion and the pillars of the earth. You have never ceased to be under the eye of Allah, being transferred through the loins of the purified and carried into the wombs of the purified women. The ignorant jāhiliyyah did not defile you, nor did the trials of vain desires involve you in shirk. You are pure, and pure is your origin. You are those through whom Allah has bestowed favor upon us, the Judge of the religion. So He placed you in houses which Allah has permitted to be raised and His name to be mentioned therein. He made our salat upon you a mercy for us and an expiation for our sins when He chose you for us and made our creation good through the grace He bestowed upon us from your wilayah. Through your grace we were, in His sight, among those who acknowledge, and through our affirming you, among those who confess.
In houses which Allah has permitted to be raised and in which His name is mentioned.

And this is the station of one who has committed excess, erred, become humbled, and confessed what he has done, and who hopes through his standing here for deliverance, and that the rescuer of those doomed from the Fire may rescue him through you. So be intercessors for me, for I have come to you when the people of the world turned away from you, took the signs of Allah in mockery, and acted arrogantly toward them.

O You who are ever-standing, who do not become heedless, everlasting, who do not become distracted, and encompassing of everything: to You belongs the favor for what You granted me of success and for making me know that with which You entrusted me, when Your servants turned away from it, were ignorant of their recognition of them, belittled their right, and inclined toward others besides them. So the favor from You was upon me along with people whom You singled out with what You singled me out with. So to You belongs all praise, since I was written before You in my station. Therefore, do not deprive me of what I hoped for, and do not disappoint me in what I supplicated for.

And supplicate for yourself with whatever you wish. Then perform eight rakʿahs in the mosque that is there, reciting in them whatever you wish, and give salām after every two rakʿahs. And it is said: it is a place in which Fāṭimah, peace be upon her, prayed.

key_terms.الْأَئِمَّةِ: the Imams, the divinely designated leaders being addressed in the visitation
key_terms.الْبَقِيعِ: al-Baqīʿ, the cemetery in Madinah where these Imams are buried
key_terms.الْمَسْجِدِ: the mosque at the site where the prescribed prayer is to be performed
key_terms.حُجَجَ اللَّهِ: the proofs of Allah, meaning His authoritative evidences over creation
key_terms.شُفَعَاءَ: intercessors, those sought for shafaʿah before Allah
key_terms.مَفْرُوضَةٌ: obligatory, describing the duty of obeying them
key_terms.وِلَايَتِكُمْ: your wilayah, their divinely granted authority and guardianship

ai.seo_question: What is the ziyārah to recite when visiting the graves of the Imams in al-Baqīʿ?
ai.summary: This text is a ziyārah and supplication for visiting the graves of the Imams buried in al-Baqīʿ, affirming their guidance, purity, and obligatory obedience. It combines testimony to their rank, confession of one’s sins, appeal for their shafaʿah, and instructions for offering salat at the site.
